short.q: Describe how Jesus responded when the disciples sent the children away.
short.answer: He told them to let the children come, said the kingdom belongs to them, and blessed them.
short.working: 1 mark for each valid point.

short.q: Explain what it means to say that love is a choice.
short.answer: We do not always feel like loving. We can still choose to be kind, like helping someone who annoyed us. Love shows in actions.
short.working: 1 mark for not always feeling, 1 for choosing kindness, 1 for example, 1 for actions.

short.q: Explain the two greatest commandments and how a child can obey them.
short.answer: Love God with all your heart, soul and mind, and love your neighbour as yourself. A child obeys by praying, reading the Bible, going to church, and by kindness, sharing and forgiving others.
short.working: 1 mark for loving God, 1 for loving neighbour, 1 for prayer or Bible, 1 for kindness, 1 for forgiving or sharing.

short.q: Name two personal items and one way of caring for each.
short.answer: Uniform: wash it; exercise book: cover it.
short.working: 1 mark for each item with care.

short.q: Give two examples of school property.
short.answer: Desks, textbooks, library books, toilets, compound.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: State three reasons why we should care for school property.
short.answer: It belongs to everyone; repair costs money; a clean school helps learning; others will use it later.
short.working: 1 mark for each reason.

short.q: Describe what a child should do when they lose or break something belonging to someone else.
short.answer: Tell the owner honestly, say sorry, offer to replace or repair it.
short.working: 1 mark for each valid step.

short.q: Explain four ways of showing responsibility at school.
short.answer: Keep the class clean, take care of books, obey rules, do assigned duties, return borrowed things.
short.working: 1 mark for each valid way up to 4.

short.q: Explain how Luke 16:10 and Genesis 2:15 teach responsibility, and give examples from school and home.
short.answer: Luke 16:10 says being faithful in small things leads to bigger tasks. Genesis 2:15 says God gave people work to do and things to care for. At school a child covers books and cleans the class. At home a child washes plates and looks after younger siblings.
short.working: 1 mark for each verse meaning, 1 for a school example, 1 for a home example, 1 for a clear link.

short.q: State two ways of glorifying God with our bodies.
short.answer: Keep clean and healthy, speak kindly, avoid harmful things, use hands to help.
short.working: 1 mark for each way.

short.q: Give two sins that do not please God.
short.answer: Lying, stealing, disobedience, bullying, jealousy.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Explain why the body is called a temple of the Holy Spirit.
short.answer: The Holy Spirit lives in believers, so the body is holy like a temple and should be treated with respect.
short.working: 1 mark for Holy Spirit, 1 for holy, 1 for respect.

short.q: Give three ways of avoiding situations that lead to sin.
short.answer: Choose good friends, avoid wrong places, be careful about what you watch, keep busy with good things, pray.
short.working: 1 mark for each way.

short.q: Describe what a child should do after sinning, in four steps.
short.answer: Admit it, say sorry to God, say sorry to the person hurt, put things right, decide not to repeat.
short.working: 1 mark for each step up to 4.

short.q: Explain why young people should lead holy lives, and give four ways of doing it.
short.answer: God is holy and asks us to be holy. Our bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit. A holy life keeps us safe and pleases God. Ways: keep clean, avoid drugs and alcohol, choose good friends, avoid harmful media, pray and read the Bible.
short.working: 1 mark for God's call, 1 for the temple idea, 1 for safety, 2 for ways.

short.q: Give two meanings of the word church.
short.answer: The building where Christians worship; the community of believers.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: State two ways of respecting the church building.
short.answer: Enter quietly, do not litter, keep phones silent, take care of Bibles.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Explain why Jesus cleared the temple.
short.answer: The temple was meant for prayer but people used it to make money and cheat. Jesus cared for the honour of His Father's house.
short.working: 1 mark for prayer purpose, 1 for making money or cheating, 1 for honour of God's house.

short.q: List three activities Christians do in church.
short.answer: Pray, sing, read the Bible, give offerings, listen to the sermon, fellowship.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Describe four ways in which children can serve in church.
short.answer: Sing in the choir, help clean, welcome visitors, read a verse, take the offering, help in Sunday school.
short.working: 1 mark for each way up to 4.

short.q: Explain the lessons that we learn from Matthew 21:12-14.
short.answer: The house of God is holy; it is for prayer; we must not misuse it or cheat others; Jesus cares about what happens there; it is a place of healing and help.
short.working: 1 mark for each valid lesson up to 5.

short.q: Name two of the twelve disciples who were brothers.
short.answer: Peter and Andrew; James and John.
short.working: 1 mark for each pair.

short.q: Explain the meaning of the word disciple.
short.answer: A follower and learner of Jesus.
short.working: 1 mark for follower and 1 for learner.

short.q: List six of the twelve disciples.
short.answer: Peter, Andrew, James, John, Philip, Bartholomew, Thomas, Matthew, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Zealot, Judas Iscariot.
short.working: 1 mark for each two correct names up to 3 marks.

short.q: State three ways in which the first Christians lived together.
short.answer: They learned the teaching, prayed, ate together, shared with the needy.
short.working: 1 mark for each valid way.

short.q: Describe how the early church began.
short.answer: The Holy Spirit came at Pentecost, Peter preached, people asked what to do, Peter told them to repent and be baptised, about three thousand believed.
short.working: 1 mark for each valid point up to 4.

short.q: Explain what it means to repent as taught in Acts 2:38 and how a child can do it.
short.answer: Repent means to be sorry for sin and turn away from it. Peter told people to repent and be baptised. A child can admit wrong, tell God sorry, ask forgiveness from others, make a decision to do better and ask the Holy Spirit's help.
short.working: 1 mark for the meaning, 1 for Acts 2:38, 1 for admitting, 1 for saying sorry, 1 for deciding to do better.

short.q: Where were believers first called Christians?
short.answer: Antioch (Acts 11:26).
short.working: 1 mark for Antioch and 1 for reference or the meaning.
